title: ScenarioFile
description:
A file of scripted scenarios for one engine (TV-010…TV-012). The provenance, the
configuration, and the named setups are given once per file; each scenario refers to a setup
and adds its own steps.

config.description: Engine configuration (managed parameters), unless a scenario gives its own.

provenance.description: Origin of the expected values, for every scenario of the file.

provenance_note.description: Derivation or cross-check details, for every scenario of the file.

setups.description: Named input sequences that reach a state, defined once and used by the scenarios.

Provenance.description: Where a vector file's expected values come from (TV-020).

oneOf.description: Example printed in a CCSDS Blue Book.
Derived by hand from the standard; `provenance_note` explains the derivation.
Agreed with an independent implementation named in `provenance_note`.

Scenario.description: One scenario: an optional setup, then its own steps.

config.description: Engine configuration that replaces the file's, for this scenario.

superseded.description: Present when this released scenario has been replaced.

ScenarioKind.description: Value of the `kind` field of an engine scenario file.

Setup.description:
A named input sequence that reaches a state. Its steps are run, with their expectations,
before the steps of a scenario that uses it.

extends.description: The setup that runs first, when this one continues it.

name.description: The name a scenario or another setup refers to; unique in the file.

Step.description: One scenario step: one input at an absolute instant, and the complete ordered outputs.

expect.description: Complete, ordered outputs expected before the next step; anything else is a failure.

expect_no_timeout.description: Expected `next_deadline` is none. Not together with `expect_timeout_us`.

expect_state.description: Expected engine state after the step; absent means not asserted (`null` is refused).

expect_timeout_us.description:
Expected `next_deadline` after the step, in microseconds; absent means not asserted
(`null` is refused). To assert that there is no deadline, set `expect_no_timeout`.

input.description: The single input of this step.

Superseded.description: Marks a released case as replaced or retired; released cases are never edited (TV-021).

by.description:
Identifier of the replacing case, if there is one. When present it must name an
existing case that is not itself superseded; a wrong case with no correct replacement
leaves it out.

reason.description: Why the case was superseded; required and not empty.
